info.title: Cloudonym API
info.description: Multi-cloud resource naming engine. This release enables Google Cloud (gcp) only; AWS and Azure are in the rule table but not enabled, and a request for them is 400 request.provider_not_enabled with the enabled providers in supported. Generates, corrects and validates resource names, one by one or for a whole project with the naming wizard (/wizard), against each provider's physical constraints. Names from /wizard may carry a tier token (web, was) after the abbreviation and kind token, and attached resources (boot and data disks, reserved addresses) are named after their server; /generate and /names never put a tier in a name. Formulas, region codes, the zones they accept, kind tokens and every rule are in /llms.txt; the resource catalog and region table are in /catalog.json (served from the site root, not under /v1). Cloudonym does not replace the provider's final verdict: it checks only the reserved words and patterns that the official documents state. Successful responses of /generate, /names, /wizard, /validate and /health carry version { engine, rules }; failures and /events do not. Every failure has the ErrorResponse shape; an unknown /v1 path or method returns 404 with code request.not_found. PASS / `valid: true` means the name satisfies the documented naming checks of this rules revision (length, pattern, reserved words). It does not mean the name is available or that you may create it — uniqueness, permissions, quotas and organisation policy are not checked. Generated names are not guaranteed unique: shortening can map two different contexts to the same name.

429.description: Too many requests from this client IP (60 per 60 seconds, shared by POST /v1/*, GET /llms.txt and GET /catalog.json). Wait the number of seconds in Retry-After. errors[0].code is request.rate_limited

post.description: Generates names and standard labels for every resource type of the requested providers from five context values. Names that cannot fit even after shortening are returned with valid=false and the reasons; nothing is silently truncated. Every violation, step and note is a Message: branch on code, show message to people. This is the catalogue: rules that need a kind (resource policies) come back valid=false here (name.kind_required); use /names with kind for them.

post.summary: Generate names for the resources you pick
post.description: Generates names for the selected resource types of one provider, count names each (sequence 01..99) or one per role, with an optional kind (a value name such as POSTGRES) whose short token goes right after the abbreviation. One request stands for one instance of each parent scope (one resource group, one project, one VPC): two items of the same kind of resource with the same name are each marked valid=false with name.conflict, and conflicts lists each collision once. Items that fail or collide are still returned with the reasons (status 200). Every violation, step and note is a Message: branch on code, show message to people.

200.description: Names for the selected resources, in request order then sequence order. data.<provider>.valid is false when any item is invalid or collides

400.description: Body is not JSON or not an object, provider is unknown or not enabled yet (request.provider_not_enabled; supported lists the enabled providers), context is invalid (including an owner, system or purpose longer than 64 characters, or an env or region longer than 1024), rules_version is not a string, or resources is invalid: not an array, empty, more than 200 items, an item that is not an object, an unknown type (supported lists the resource types), a duplicate type, count not an integer from 1 to 99, count above 1 or a role on a rule that takes none, a role not matching ^[a-z0-9]{2,16}$, a kind on a rule that takes none (selection.kind_not_supported), a kind that is not one of the rule's values (selection.unknown_kind; params.supported lists them), no kind on a rule that needs one (selection.kind_required; params.supported), or more than 200 names in total (selection.* codes)

post.summary: Name a whole project: project-level resources and one or more services
post.description: The naming wizard. One request is one GCP project: the project ID (always the first item), project-level resources (project_picks: network, firewall rules) and, per service (purpose), the resources picked from presets or by rule id. Servers keep their sequence number (instances[].seq), so removing server 01 does not rename server 02. A server can carry attached resources (boot disk, data disks, a static external or internal address) whose names are the server name plus a suffix (-boot, -data-01, -ip, -ipi); they are never shortened. Items are returned in order: project level, then each service, each parent followed by its attached resources. Item keys are structured paths (service/shop/compute_instance/web/01/data/01). Items that fail or collide are still returned with the reasons (status 200). The response is reproduced by repeating the same wizard request with its rules_version; /names is a separate, flat endpoint.

200.description: Names for the whole project, in structured-key order. data.<provider>.valid is false when any item is invalid or collides

400.description: Body is not JSON or not an object, provider is unknown or not enabled yet, project is not an object, a context value or purpose is invalid or too long (field project.owner, services[1].purpose ...), or the wizard plan is invalid (wizard.* and selection.* codes). field is the request path of the offending element, in request names: services[1].picks[0].instances[1].attach.data[0], project_picks[2], services[1]. Errors about the whole plan (wizard.empty, wizard.too_many_services, wizard.too_many_names, selection.not_array for services or project_picks) have no field

env.description: Canonical: prod, stg, dev, sbx. Common aliases are accepted and normalised (prd, production, live -> prod; staging -> stg; development -> dev; sandbox -> sbx).

region.description: A region or a zone of the provider, by name or by code (asia-northeast3, asia-northeast3-a, ane3, ane3a), or global. Names carry the region code (ane3); a zone name is accepted and resolved to its region, so zonal resources are named like regional ones. Country values and region names of another provider are 400 context.value_unsupported with candidates in supported. The region table is in /llms.txt.

providers.description: Omit for every enabled provider (only gcp for now; aws and azure are planned). Must be non-empty when present. A known provider that is not enabled yet is 400 request.provider_not_enabled.

rules_version.description: Optional pin to a rules revision (YYYY-MM-DD.N). If it differs from the current revision the API answers 409 instead of returning names that may differ. Not a string -> 400.

data.description: provider -> resource_type -> ResourceItem. The provider set equals the requested providers.

generated_labels.description: provider -> standard tags/labels (owner, system, purpose, environment, managed_by)

label_violations.description: provider -> label values over the provider's limit or with characters the provider rejects (values are never truncated)

label_transformed.description: provider -> label values changed to fit the provider's character rules (GCP)

transformed.description: Context values normalised from aliases (context.normalized, e.g. env 'production' -> 'prod')

name.description: Final name. Empty when a required token became empty after normalisation.

valid.description: PASS / `valid: true` means the name satisfies the documented naming checks of this rules revision (length, pattern, reserved words). It does not mean the name is available or that you may create it — uniqueness, permissions, quotas and organisation policy are not checked. Generated names are not guaranteed unique: shortening can map two different contexts to the same name.

resources.description: The resource types to name, each at most once. The total number of names (sum of count) is at most 200. The limits are for one screen and one share link; they do not bound the response size.

type.description: A resource_type of the provider (see /llms.txt Resource tree)

count.description: Only on rules with a sequence number (input count). Default 1

role.description: Only on role rules (input role). Default sync

kind.description: Only on rules with a kind table (see /llms.txt Kind tokens): a value name of that rule, such as POSTGRES or snapshot-schedule, not the token. The value that is the provider default for that scope adds no token. Required on resource_policy

rules_version.description: Optional pin to a rules revision (YYYY-MM-DD.N). If it differs from the current revision the API answers 409 instead of returning names that may differ. Not a string -> 400.

data.description: provider -> NamesProviderResult. Exactly one key: the requested provider.

valid.description: true only when every item is valid (after name.conflict is applied)

conflicts.description: One name.conflict per collision (params.name, params.keys). The same message is also in the violations of each colliding item

NameItem.description: One generated name of /names: a ResourceItem with the item key, resource type, sequence or role, kind, placement scope and uniqueness

key.description: Unique within the response: resource_type_seq (count rules), resource_type_role (role rules) or resource_type (rules with no input)

role.description: Present on role rules: the requested role or the default sync

kind.description: Present when the item asked for a kind: the value name as sent

kind_token.description: Present when the kind puts a token in the name (absent for the provider default of that scope)

scope.description: scope is the placement scope: the parent the resource is created in (a scope id such as azure:resource_group). It says where the name lives, not that the provider enforces uniqueness there; see uniqueness.

uniqueness.description: uniqueness "csp" means the provider requires the name to be unique within its scope; "none" (AWS Name tags) means the provider does not enforce uniqueness at all. Cloudonym compares names only with each other inside one request (name.conflict), never with resources that already exist.

instances.description: One slot per server (rules with a sequence number only). Required on those rules

attach.description: Attached resources (virtual machines only): boot disk, data disks, static external (ip) and internal (ipi) address
